findings.source_evidence: The source defines a fractional-step finite-volume method on rectangular or logically rectangular grids through sequential one-dimensional coordinate solves and retains cases needing a fully multidimensional method.
findings.translation_evidence: The reconstruction proves only that folding [xDirectionSolve,yDirectionSolve] applies two arbitrary endomorphisms in list order.
findings.impact: The theorem holds for unrelated functions on any type and does not characterize dimensional splitting, its grid applicability, its fractional-step nature, or its limits.

rationale: The reconstruction captures only the syntax of sequential composition. Because its definitional fold equality is universally true while all finite-volume, PDE, grid, fractional-step, and adequacy content is missing, it is strictly weaker.
